paths.description: Unknown-route HTTP behavior plus manifest/service-worker/offline capability inspection.

findings.summary: The public experience stays light when the user requests a dark color scheme.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot remains white and home-probe.json reports colorScheme normal, a white body background, no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and map surfaces, text, controls, and browser chrome through preference-aware color tokens.

findings.summary: A large consent panel interrupts every audited public route and obscures primary content.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, listing, story, search, and login screenshots show a first-load panel for 1,013 partners covering a substantial portion of the viewport. The probe identifies a custom DIV role=dialog without aria-modal.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, semantic consent dialog with focus containment, equal accept/reject prominence, persistent choice, and no repeated obstruction after a decision.

findings.summary: Numerous interactive targets are smaller than a robust touch target.
findings.evidence: The objective DOM probe counted 19 visible controls below 24px on both home and story, and 15 on login. Lighthouse accessibility was 0.97 but does not negate these measured target dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase hit areas to at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, preferably 44 by 44 for primary mobile controls, while preserving visible focus.

findings.summary: The homepage is slow and shifts beyond the good CLS range in the tested mobile profile.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 6.8s, FCP 5.1s, TTI 21.9s, and CLS 0.117. The mobile layout primitive independently measured CLS 0.136, including a 0.106 shift around 3.8s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP element, reserve all late content space, shorten critical chains, and defer non-essential scripts until after the primary content is usable.

findings.summary: The landing page ships a heavy, script-rich dependency graph with substantial unused code.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 203 requests and 3.94MB transferred, including 82 scripts and 93 images. Lighthouse reported 4,174KiB total, about 449KiB unused JS, 41KiB unused CSS, and 2.7s main-thread work.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split first-party code, delay analytics/ads/identity SDKs until needed or consented, remove unused CSS, and keep the critical path to essential content only.

findings.summary: Some controls do not expose a reliable accessible name.
findings.evidence: The home probe found unlabeled search inputs and many image-only cover links without textual or ARIA naming; Lighthouse also failed label-content-name-mismatch.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each control a programmatic name matching its visible purpose; associate search labels and name cover links from the story title.

findings.summary: Some text does not meet minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse/axe color-contrast audit failed on the tested homepage. Forced-colors rendering remained usable, so this finding is limited to authored color pairs in normal mode.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust the failing foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA and verify hover, disabled, and muted-text states.

findings.summary: Key entry pages omit a level-one heading and use inconsistent landmark structure.
findings.evidence: home-probe.json reports zero h1 elements and starts the visual hero at h2; login-probe.json also reports zero h1. The story detail correctly has one h1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one descriptive h1 for each page purpose and keep a logical heading hierarchy and main landmark across both modern and legacy templates.

findings.summary: Image delivery causes stability, clarity, and bandwidth problems.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 98/100 images without explicit dimensions, 38 oversized, 25 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, and 91 legacy-format assets. Lighthouse failed aspect-ratio and responsive-image audits.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, provide responsive srcset/sizes, use modern formats where supported, and lazy-load non-critical images.

findings.summary: Share-preview metadata is incomplete on representative public pages.
findings.evidence: The homepage and story probes found no Open Graph properties; the story has JSON-LD, while the organization/home entity has no JSON-LD.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter metadata to public pages and Organization/WebSite JSON-LD to the homepage, matching visible titles, descriptions, and images.

findings.summary: Important browser security defenses and cookie attributes are missing.
findings.evidence: headers.json reports no CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. cookies.json reports 18 flagged cookies, including non-Secure analytics and host cookies and broad SameSite=None usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure and use Lax/Strict unless cross-site behavior is essential.

findings.summary: The first-load third-party and tracking footprint is disproportionate.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe saw 16 third-party origins and four known trackers. HAR attributed 90 requests and 2.18MB to third-party origins, while the consent UI names 1,013 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to minimal first-party analytics, gate all non-essential vendors behind consent, remove redundant trackers, and batch/defer telemetry.

findings.summary: The visible authentication choices do not offer a first-party phishing-resistant passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login screen offers Google, Facebook, and email/password. The email probe exposed username and password fields but no passkey action, despite browser WebAuthn support.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration and authentication alongside federated and recovery options, with conditional UI where supported.

findings.summary: The app-like reading service exposes neither installability metadata nor an offline fallback.
findings.evidence: Home and story probes found no web app manifest and no controlling service worker on representative app/content routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a manifest and a service worker that preserves a useful offline shell and previously saved reading content, with clear stale/offline status.

findings.summary: An unknown route is interpreted as a user profile and returns a malformed recovery page.
findings.evidence: The unknown-route request redirects to /user/this-route-does-not-exist-web-uplift, then returns HTTP 404 with the generic homepage title and an h1 aria-label of “s profile”.
findings.suggestedFix: Render a dedicated 404 state with a descriptive title, clear explanation, search/home actions, and no malformed user-profile semantics.

findings.summary: Locale-sensitive content is rendered as fixed English text without semantic time markup.
findings.evidence: The global story page renders “Tue, Dec 2, 2025” but story-probe.json finds no time elements, while the site advertises language selection and global reach.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit semantic datetime values and format dates, durations, and numbers with Intl using the selected locale.

findings.summary: The email login fields omit autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: login-email-probe.json reports required username and password controls with empty autocomplete values. Empty submission uses clear native validation, so this finding is specifically about input assistance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete="username" and autocomplete="current-password", and preserve password-manager and paste support.
